output.brief: The remote promotion gap is mostly a difference in who is eligible, not where people work. Only 32% of remote staff have the 18 months in level that the policy requires, against 74% of office staff. Among eligible people, nomination rates (28% vs 29%), approval rates (71% vs 74%) and overall promotion rates (20% vs 21%) are almost the same. Applying office rates to the remote eligibility mix predicts 8.2%, and the observed rate is 7.6%. The headline gap therefore mostly reflects tenure. The remaining 1.1-point difference rests on only 110 people, so a real small effect of proximity can't be ruled out. Managers' comments hint at informal favouritism in who gets visible work, but our staffing data can't measure this. I'm fairly confident, but not certain. Don't announce the three-day office rule. It rests on the wrong comparison, and it would penalise the roughly 180 staff hired on home-based contracts. Next steps: put the rule on hold, change the dashboard to compare eligible employees only, and track stretch-work allocation so you can re-check at FY2027. Also find out why remote staff are newer (hiring mix or attrition).
